answer:
The sequence \((a_n)\) is defined recursively by \(a_0 = 1\), \(a_1 = \sqrt[19]{2}\), and \(a_n = a_{n-1} \cdot a_{n-2}^2\) for \(n \geq 2\). We need to find the smallest positive integer \(k\) such that the product \(a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k\) is an integer.

First, we express each term \(a_n\) as a power of 2. Let \(a_n = 2^{b_n/19}\). The recurrence relation translates to \(b_n = b_{n-1} + 2b_{n-2}\) with initial conditions \(b_0 = 0\) and \(b_1 = 1\).

We need the sum \(S_k = b_1 + b_2 + \cdots + b_k\) to be divisible by 19. We compute the terms \(b_n\) and their partial sums \(S_k\) modulo 19:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
n & b_n \mod 19 & S_k \mod 19 \\
\hline
1 & 1 & 1 \\
2 & 1 & 2 \\
3 & 3 & 5 \\
4 & 5 & 10 \\
5 & 11 & 21 \equiv 2 \\
6 & 2 & 4 \\
7 & 5 & 9 \\
8 & 9 & 18 \\
9 & 0 & 18 \\
10 & 18 & 36 \equiv 17 \\
11 & 18 & 35 \equiv 16 \\
12 & 16 & 32 \equiv 13 \\
13 & 14 & 27 \equiv 8 \\
14 & 8 & 16 \\
15 & 17 & 33 \equiv 14 \\
16 & 14 & 28 \equiv 9 \\
17 & 10 & 19 \equiv 0 \\
\end{array}
\]

The first occurrence where \(S_k \equiv 0 \mod 19\) is at \(k = 17\). Therefore, the smallest positive integer \(k\) such that the product \(a_1 a_2 \cdots a_k\) is an integer is \(\boxed{17}\).
